name: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest active-equity mutual fund house by market share (active equity 12.7%, overall QAAUM share 11.1%), 52.3% owned by HDFC Bank. Q2 FY27: QAAUM Rs9.69 lakh cr (+10% y/y, +4% q/q), equity-oriented QAAUM Rs6.51 lakh cr, revenue ~Rs1,170cr (+14% y/y), PAT ~Rs750cr (+4% y/y), operating margin ~79%. Asset-light, debt-free, 79% payout, ROE 33%. Earnings are a function of AUM x fee yield (~47-48bp blended): driven by equity markets, SIP flows, market share and SEBI fee rules (new regulations effective 1 Apr 2026). P/E 37.9, 13x book, dividend yield 2.1%.

exposures.mechanism: Industry equity AUM grows via SIP + lump-sum. SIP inflows ~Rs3.9 lakh cr/yr (Rs32,297cr in Aug 2026 record; Rs325bn Sep per company deck) ~9% of equity AUM; +10% => equity AUM growth +0.9pp/yr; HDFC AMC share 12.7% flows; equity ~75% of revenue (yield ~58bp active equity vs ~48bp blended) => revenue +0.7%, PBT +0.8%/yr, compounding 3 yrs, structural flow persistence 0.7 at 38x P/E => +2.5. SIP AUM was flat q/q in Sep (MOFSL) - watch.

evidence.note: MOFSL: QAAUM Rs9.69 lakh cr (+10% y/y), active equity share 12.7% (-10bp q/q), SIP AUM flat q/q

exposures.mechanism: +20% traded value/demat additions => retail participation up, equity MF lump-sum and SIP registrations +~5%; revenue +~1.5% (equity-weighted) => PBT +1.8% x persistence 0.5-1.0 x multiple => ~+2.0.

+US$5bn/qtr FPI inflow ~ +3% Nifty (beta 1.39) => equity-oriented QAAUM (Rs6.5 lakh cr, 67% of total) +3.5% mark-to-market => revenue +2.6% => PBT +3.1% x persistence 0.5 => +1.5 (before market demeaning). FIIs hold 24.1%.

evidence.note: MOFSL: QAAUM Rs9.69 lakh cr (+10% y/y), active equity share 12.7% (-10bp q/q), SIP AUM flat q/q

exposures.mechanism: +5 VIX points ~ -3-4% equities => AUM -2.5% => revenue -2% => PBT -2.4% x 0.5 x EV/MCap 0.97 => ~-1.2 gross; pack residual -0.40 (t -1.1) after controlling for market; take -0.8.

Higher LTCG/STCG on equity funds cuts after-tax returns and retail inflows; 2024 Budget hike precedent. +1 => net flows -10% => AUM growth -0.9pp/yr (mirror of flows edge) => -2.5. Union Budget 1 Feb 2027 is the next window; probability of a rise modest.
Tighter F&O rules (lot sizes, weekly expiry curbs) push retail savers from leveraged trading to SIPs/MFs; +1 step => SIP registrations +2% => +0.8. Substitution evidence limited.

Further TER / brokerage / fee-structure tightening beyond the 1 Apr 2026 reset (brokerage caps 6bp cash / 2bp derivatives; TER slabs partly offset +5bp). SSU: -5bp on active-equity gross yield. 5bp / 58bp = -8.6% of equity revenue (75% of total) = -6.5% revenue; costs fixed => PBT -8%; mitigation (cost cuts, mix) 35% => ~-5. Jefferies sized the April 2026 change at -8-10% FY27 PBT (draft) and the stock rallied up to 8.5% on the final rules (2025-12-18), i.e. largely priced.

evidence.note: SEBI MF Regulations 2026 effective 1 Apr 2026: brokerage caps 6bp/2bp, TER restructure; Jefferies FY27 PBT -8-10% (draft), Centrum -6-10%

exposures.mechanism: P/E 37.9x (P/B 13x): very long duration; +25bp G-sec => ~-2.5% on multiple at 50% CoE pass-through. Debt+liquid ~26% of QAAUM at lower fees; higher yields hurt bond-fund NAVs and the ~Rs8,000cr treasury float marginally. Pack residual vs Fed funds +1.83 (t 1.3) not significant.

evidence.note: India 10y G-sec ~7.4-7.5% in Oct 2026, multi-year high (Reuters/ET headlines); Nov outlook 7.25-7.35%

exposures.mechanism: Structural shift of household savings into MFs: +1 = industry AUM growth +2pp/yr for 3 yrs => HDFC AMC revenue +~6% cumulative at stable share and yield => PBT +7% => capitalised with persistence 0.7 => +4. SIP AUM +14% y/y, QAAUM +10% y/y shows the trend is intact but slowing (MOFSL).

evidence.note: MOFSL: QAAUM Rs9.69 lakh cr (+10% y/y), active equity share 12.7% (-10bp q/q), SIP AUM flat q/q

exposures.mechanism: SSU: +1 = 0.5pp loss of active-equity AUM market share to new entrants (passives, discount brokers, Jio-style entrants, bank-owned AMCs). 0.5/12.7 = -3.9% equity AUM => -3% revenue => -3.7% PBT; persistence 1.0 (structural) => -3.5. Share slipped 10bp q/q and 20bp y/y to 12.7% in Q2 (MOFSL).

evidence.note: MOFSL: QAAUM Rs9.69 lakh cr (+10% y/y), active equity share 12.7% (-10bp q/q), SIP AUM flat q/q

exposures.mechanism: Debt/liquid ~26% of QAAUM (fee yield ~15-25bp). Hikes cut bond-fund returns and shift savers to FDs (-) but lift liquid-fund yields and inflows (+). Net small: -0.3.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (The Hindu, Reuters headlines)

Weight small because AMC earnings are driven by AUM. (The reverse stake edge HDFCAMC->HDFCBANK is ~0.04 per +1% and belongs in the bank profile.)
